criteria.long_description: A tessellation with at least 12 complete tiles that fit together with no gaps or overlaps, is neatly and clearly drawn, and uses at least two different types of symmetry (reflection, rotation or translation).

ratings.long_description: At least 12 complete tiles, no gaps or overlaps, neat and clear, and at least two symmetry types present.
Meets the requirements except for one small problem, such as a few untidy edges or a tile count just under 12.
Has gaps or overlaps, fewer than 12 tiles, or only one symmetry type.
No tessellation submitted.

criteria.long_description: Questions 1-3: the tile shape or shapes described precisely, why they tessellate (angle sum at a vertex), and the symmetries of a single tile.

ratings.long_description: Describes the tile(s) precisely, explains with angle measures why they tessellate, and states each tile's lines of reflection symmetry and order of rotational symmetry correctly.
All three questions answered, with one imprecise or partly incorrect explanation.
One question is missing or most answers are vague or incorrect.
Section not completed.

criteria.description: Part 2, Section B: Symmetries of Your Tessellation
criteria.long_description: Questions 4-6: a translation vector with direction and distance, the second symmetry type described specifically (line of symmetry, or center, angle and order of rotation), and the third type identified or its absence explained.

ratings.long_description: Gives a translation vector with direction and distance, describes the second symmetry with its line or center and angle, and handles the third type correctly, all specific to the student's design.
All three questions answered, but one lacks detail (for example, no distance or no center or angle stated).
One question is missing, or the answers are generic or partly incorrect.
Section not completed.

criteria.description: Part 2, Section C: Reflection and Connection, and Mathematical Language
criteria.long_description: Questions 7-8: how a single tile's symmetries relate to the whole pattern, and whether translation symmetry guarantees other symmetries, supported with evidence from the design. Uses correct vocabulary (line of symmetry, order and angle of rotational symmetry, translation vector, tessellation) and answers are specific to the design, not generic.

ratings.long_description: Both questions answered with specific evidence from the design, and the required vocabulary is used correctly throughout.
Both questions answered, but the evidence is thin or the vocabulary is used loosely in places.
One question is missing, or the answers are generic and could describe any tessellation.
Section not completed.

source.note: Built 2026-10-23 from the reformatted Geometry course (HSGeometryHonors/02_Design Q3-Q4 Module Formatted folders; Module 9 is split across the two quarters in the formatted set and is one module here). Module and item titles, order, sub-headers, points, grading types, submission types and Wiris LTI links (quiz id + lookup uuid) were read from the product master copy export (10th-grade-geometry-product-master-copy-export.imscc): the course was never deployed to Canvas the old way and has no Module Maps in the formatted set, so the export is the naming authority. This is the Honors course (1206320), so items marked Honors Only are included. The five Module Lesson Maps pages are in an unpublished Teacher Resources module. The export's teacher bucket also holds rubric and answer-key pages for the construction assignments; the answer keys were never formatted or published and are not in this kit. The six construction rubrics (Lessons 7.03b, 7.06b x3, 7.07 x2) are native Canvas rubrics converted word for word from those rubric pages (three criteria on a 0-3 scale, total 9), with points scaled to the assignment: doubled for the 18-point assignments, and weighted 7/7/6 for Lesson 7.03b (20 points). The Lesson 10.07 Tessellation assignment has no rubric in the source; its rubric was written on 2026-10-23 from the assignment's own requirements and scoring note. Lesson 9.04 Independent Practice (70 points, 14 points for each of five triangles per its own scoring summary) has a rubric page in the export that grades one triangle, which a single Canvas rubric cannot express, so it carries no native rubric. Lessons and assignment pages are on https://optimaondemand.github.io/hs-geometry-honors and the twelve lesson videos on https://optimaondemand.github.io/hs-geometry-honors-videos. Gradebook groups and weights (40/40/20) from the course owner; construction and project assignments count in Practice & Checks, and Review of Transformations in Reviews & VR; the course's teacher manual recommends four groups (45/20/25/10). The bundled syllabus is a PDF rendered from the course's HTML; the teacher manual is the course's PDF. No week pacing exists in the course files, so no item carries a week.
